content:
alex: Heads-up — I hit a subtle parity issue between the REST API and the JS SDK when forwarding custom headers (auth/retry flow). @maria can you help triage?

maria: ugh, details? quick repro? :eyes:

alex: Minimal repro: curl with a client-request-id header behaves as expected (server echoes header, retry middleware dedupes), but the same call via the SDK loses the header so retries are treated as new requests.

alex: curl example:
```
curl -i -X POST \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Request-Id: abc-123" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hi"}'
```

alex: Node SDK call (what we tried):
```js
// pseudo
await client.text.generate({model: 'rwd-small', input: 'hi'}, {
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, 'x-client-request-id': 'abc-123' }
})
```

alex: Observed: REST request shows X-Client-Request-Id on server logs. SDK request does not. Retry logic treated retried attempts as new because header missing.

jonathan: I remember we sanitize headers in the SDK http layer and only forward an allowlist (content-type, authorization, accept, user-agent). Looks like x-client-request-id wasn't whitelisted. That was intentional to avoid leaking internal headers, but it breaks customers trying to attach idempotency or tracing ids.

maria: two separate issues then: 1) default header whitelist is too restrictive for customer tracing/idempotency, 2) header casing/normalization behavior differs and the SDK may be lowercasing and dropping unknown keys. Both affect parity.

sam: Also noticed the SDK transforms `authorization` value if it's missing the `Bearer ` prefix — it prepends `Bearer `, while some internal infra sends raw API keys in a different header. Could cause mismatches when teams pass a token in `x-api-key` expecting passthrough.

alex: Proposed fix: make headers opt-out instead of opt-in — forward any user-provided headers unless they match redwood-internal blacklist (eg: x-internal-token). Add a small integration test: client -> proxy -> echo headers; assert user headers survive.

jonathan: agreed. I'll open an issue + branch. Will keep default safe by still blocking obviously sensitive internal headers, but forward all others. Also add a note in SDK README about header passthrough behavior.

jonathan: creating issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3421 (PR incoming: sdk/headers-pass-through)

alex: Nice. For immediate customer unblock, can we add a middleware that copies provided headers into the request options and sets `x-client-request-id` explicitly? Might be quicker until PR lands.

maria: yes — add a compatibility middleware and ship a patch to npm with a test. I'll take the patch.

sdk-bot: deploy bot: patch release 0.12.3 published for @redwood/sdk-js (chore: header passthrough middleware)

sam: thx! Can we also add an e2e that verifies retry dedupe by header so we don't regress?

jonathan: will add it to the PR. assigning to @maria and @jonathan.

alex: thanks everyone — leaving the repro and logs in the issue. :white_check_mark:
